---
title: "Connecting to Unity"
---

## What is Unity?

Unity is the high-performance computing cluster we use to run analyses that are too large for a personal laptop. For RNA-seq, Unity gives us access to more storage, more memory, and more computing power.

Most of the work in this tutorial happens in a terminal after you log in to Unity.

## Before you start

You will need:

- A Unity account
- Your Unity username
- An internet connection
- A terminal application
- Duo or another multi-factor authentication method, if required by your account

On macOS, you can use the built-in Terminal app. On Windows, you can use PowerShell, Windows Terminal, or an SSH client.

## Connect with SSH

From your terminal, run:

```bash
ssh your_username@unity.rc.umass.edu
```

Replace `your_username` with your own Unity username.

For example:

```bash
ssh kfloer_smith_edu@unity.rc.umass.edu
```

Example output:

```text
The authenticity of host 'unity.rc.umass.edu' can't be established.
Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no/[fingerprint])?
```

If this is your first time connecting, type:

```text
yes
```

Then enter your password and complete multi-factor authentication if prompted.

## Check where you are

After logging in, your terminal prompt should change. It may look something like this:

```text
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$
```

This means you are on a Unity login node.

Run:

```bash
hostname
```

Example output:

```text
login1
```

## Important login node rule

The login node is for light work only, such as:

- Editing files
- Moving files
- Checking directories
- Submitting jobs
- Starting interactive sessions

Do not run large RNA-seq analyses directly on the login node.

::: {.callout-warning}
nf-core pipelines can use a lot of CPU, memory, and disk space. Run pipeline work through the appropriate Unity compute resources, not directly on the login node.
:::

## Disconnect from Unity

When you are finished, run:

```bash
exit
```

Example output:

```text
logout
Connection to unity.rc.umass.edu closed.
```
